column1: # Routes of the papers' proofs: the numbered results each proof cites.
# Generated by route_check.py extract from prefixed copies of the TeX sources (D: = dense paper,
# Theory of Computing 2023 version; S: = sparse paper, arXiv:2302.05605v2), then edited by hand

# Theorem 1.6 is proved in running text: Lemma 2.1 is Part 1, Lemmas 3.5, 3.6, 3.3 are Parts 2, 3, 4 (end of Section 3: "These lemmas and Lemma 3.3, together with Lemma 2.1 form the complete chain of shrinking").
# Lemma 2.1 is proved in the subsection "Proof of Lemma 2.1": Claims 2.5 and 2.6 and Chebyshev's inequality.
# Lemma 2.3 (TeX label `thm:diff of binom r.v. gen.`, renamed because of its spaces).
# Lemma 2.4 (TeX label `thm:1/sqrt{n}`, renamed because of its braces): "by the same computations in Lemma 2.3", i.e. the application of Theorem 2.2 in that proof.
# Appendix A proves a delayed version of Theorem 1.4 (FKM) from Theorem 1.5; it is a section, not a statement, so the extractor does not attribute its proof.
# Theorem 1.2 is proved in running text, subsection "Wrapping up the proof of Theorem 1.2".
# Theorem 1.4 has no label; S:thm:delayed-FKM is the formalization's. Its proof follows it (unattributed by the extractor).
# Theorem 1.5 has no label; S:thm:biased-coloring is the formalization's. It is proved in the paragraph after it.
# Theorem 1.7 follows from Theorem 4.1 ("which can be readily seen to imply Theorem 1.7").
# Lemma 2.1 is proved in running text right after Proposition 2.2 ("Assume, for now, Proposition 2.2 ... Chebyshev's inequality implies").

# Theorem 3.1 uses Steps 1-2 of the proof of Theorem 1.2 (Lemmas 2.1, 2.4) and "the first half of the proof of Lemma 2.6" (Lemmas 2.5, A.7); it cites Lemma A.4 only to say that it does not apply below the threshold. It also uses the period-two theorem of Goles-Olivos and Poljak-Sura (cited, unlabelled).
# Theorem 4.1 is proved by Propositions 4.2, 4.3 and 4.4 ("Our proof consists of three main propositions").
# Proposition 4.2 also cites the proof of Theorem 1.2, only for the numerical values of D_c and C(c, D).
# Proposition 4.4 has no label; S:prop:lazy-final is the formalization's.
# Theorem A.1 is the same cited theorem as the dense paper's Theorem 2.2 (D:thm:esseen).
# Corollary A.2 "naturally follow[s]" from Theorem A.1 (Berry-Esseen); both papers cite the same theorem, whose formal hypothesis carries the label D:thm:esseen.
